19-074.r: Ministries at the Centre on 15 August 1947 → 18; at present → 53 (not 36).

19-075.r: Ministry of Tribal Affairs → set up in 1999 by bifurcating the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, for focused development of Scheduled Tribes.

19-076.r: Narayan Desai → Chairman of War Resisters International (anti-war body, founded 1921 at Bilthoven, Netherlands; HQ London) from 1988 to 1991.

19-077.r: Nagendra Singh → President, International Court of Justice (1985-1988); A.N. Roy → Chief Justice of India (1973); R.K. Trivedi → Chief Election Commissioner; Ashok Desai → Attorney-General.

19-078.r: UIDAI (created June 2009): first Director General → Ram Sewak Sharma; first Chairman → Nandan Nilekani.
19-078.t: Don't confuse the first DG (R.S. Sharma) with the first Chairman (Nandan Nilekani).

19-079.r: Sarosh Zaiwalla → renowned international (arbitration) law expert; former member, ICC International Court of Arbitration, Paris (1990-2002); got National Law Day Award.

19-080.r: After 18th Lok Sabha elections → Giriraj Singh (MP from Begusarai, Bihar) made Union Minister of Textiles in Modi government.

19-081.r: Minister of Minority Affairs (at question time) → Smriti Irani (MoS John Barla); Ministry carved out of Social Justice and Empowerment on 29 January 2006.

19-082.r: White Paper → official Government of India document explaining policy on a subject, used to get feedback before a bill is prepared.

19-083.r: Reorganisation of the Union Cabinet → based on the report of N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.

19-084.r: Cabinet Secretariat → works directly under the PM (not Vice-President); its head, the Cabinet Secretary → ex-officio Chairman of Civil Services Board, highest civil servant of Centre.

19-086.r: Cabinet Secretariat functions → Cabinet agenda, secretariat help to Cabinet and its Committees, Rules of Business, inter-ministerial coordination; NOT allocating funds to Ministries (Allocation of Business Rules, 1961).

19-087.r: Split system in Indian administration → separation of Policy-making from Implementation, for efficiency in both.

19-088.r: President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) → Prime Minister of India.

19-089.r: National Defence Committee → headed by the Prime Minister.

19-090.r: Office of Parliamentary Secretary in independent India → book's answer 1952; its explanation says the office was created in 1951.
19-090.c: Printed answer (b) 1952 contradicts the explanation, which says 1951.

19-091.r: Wrong pair: Rajiv Gandhi → Veer Bhumi, not Karma Bhumi (Shankar Dayal Sharma, ninth President); Nehru → Shanti Van; Shastri → Vijay Ghat; Indira → Shakti Sthal.

19-092.r: 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' → Lal Bahadur Shastri, 1965, at Ramlila Maidan, Delhi, during the Indo-Pak War.

20-001.r: Art 76 → Attorney General advises Government of India on legal matters; first law officer; appointed by President, holds office during President's pleasure.

20-004.r: Attorney General (Art 76) → appointed by the President, holds office at his pleasure (no security of tenure); highest/first law officer of India.
20-004.t: Not appointed by the Law Minister or PM; only the President appoints and removes him.

20-007.r: Chief legal adviser to Government of India → Attorney General (Art 76), part of Union Executive; has right of audience in all courts of India.
20-007.t: Don't confuse with Solicitor General (second law officer) or Advocate General (State).

20-010.r: Government's chief legal adviser and main lawyer in Supreme Court → Attorney General (Art 76); not Solicitor General, CJI or CAG → 'None of the above'.

20-011.r: AG must be qualified as SC judge (Art 124(3)): HC judge five years, HC advocate ten years, or eminent jurist; not removed like SC judges, serves at President's pleasure.

20-012.r: Art 76(1) → AG must be qualified to be appointed a Supreme Court Judge; Art 76(4) → holds office during the pleasure of the President.
20-012.t: Not 'qualified as a High Court Judge'; that is the Advocate General of a State.

20-013.r: AG: appointed by President; same qualifications as SC judge; need not be an MP; removed by President, not impeached; speaks in Parliament (Art 88) but no vote.

20-014.r: AG → qualified to be SC judge (Art 76(1)); remuneration determined by the President, not Parliament (Art 76(4)); holds office at President's pleasure.

20-015.r: Attorney General (Art 76) → holds office at President's pleasure, not PM's; speaks in both Houses but cannot vote; Constitution doesn't require him to resign with the government.
20-015.c: The book says (a) Only 2, but its explanation never addresses MP privileges; the standard answer is (b) Neither 1 nor 2, since the Constitution gives the AG the privileges of an MP.

20-017.r: Attorney General → can speak and take part in either House, joint sitting and Parliamentary committees (Art 88), but cannot vote; CAG reports laid before Parliament (Art 151).
20-017.h: AG = Allowed to talk, not Granted a vote.

20-023.r: AG: advises on legal matters referred by President; audience in all courts (Art 76(3)); speaks in Parliament, no vote (Art 88); not full-time counsel, may practise privately.

20-024.r: Non-members in Parliament's proceedings → Attorney General (both Houses) and Vice-President (Rajya Sabha only) → 'more than one'; for 'both Houses' the answer is AG.

20-026.r: Non-member taking part in a House of Parliament → Vice-President (Rajya Sabha) and Attorney General (either House); book accepts both (a) and (c).
20-026.c: Printed answer is (a) only, but the explanation says '& (c)', i.e. both (a) and (c).

20-027.r: Solicitor General → legal adviser; second law officer, subordinate to and assists the Attorney General; helped by Additional Solicitor Generals.

20-029.r: State's legal adviser → Advocate General (Art 165): appointed by Governor, qualified as HC judge (165(1)); advises State (165(2)); holds office at Governor's pleasure (165(3)).

20-032.r: Art 165(2) → Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters; holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not the Cabinet.

20-034.r: CAG → appointed by President by warrant (Art 148(1)); removed like SC judge; Union audit reports → President; State audit reports → Governor.
hi: Comptroller and Auditor General (नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक)

20-039.r: CAG salary and service conditions → Part E of the Second Schedule; CAG appointed under Art 148; head of Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

20-040.r: CAG term → 6 years or age 65, whichever earlier (CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971); service conditions set by Parliament (Art 148(3)).

20-042.r: Not true: 'CAG removed by the President' at will; removed only like an SC judge (Art 148(1)); salary equals SC judge; no further government office (148(4)).
20-042.t: Removal order is signed by the President, but only after Parliament's address, as for an SC judge.

20-044.r: CAG checks not just legality but also propriety of expenditure, as he upholds the Constitution and Parliament's laws in financial administration; he does NOT control issue of public money.

20-047.r: CAG reports → discussed by Public Accounts Committee; investigating agencies can press charges using them; CAG has no exchequer control in emergency and no judicial powers.

20-048.r: Final action on CAG's comments → Parliament (via Public Accounts Committee); Art 151(1): Union audit reports go to President, then laid before Parliament.

20-049.r: CAG attends meetings of Parliament's Public Accounts Committee; CAG's duties and powers → Article 149.

20-051.r: CAG Articles: 148 → appointment; 149 → duties and powers; 150 → form of accounts of Union and States; 151 → audit reports.
20-051.h: 148-151 in order: Appoint, Duties, Form, Reports.

20-052.r: CAG removed like an SC judge (Art 148(1), 124(4)) → by President after an address by both Houses (special majority) for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

20-053.r: Not true: CAG office expenses 'voted' → they are charged on Consolidated Fund of India (Art 148(6)); CAG barred from later government office (148(4)); removed like SC judge.
hi: Consolidated Fund of India (भारत की संचित निधि)

20-054.r: CAG → 'Friend, Philosopher and Guide' of the Public Accounts Committee; attends PAC sittings and assists its deliberations.

20-055.r: Power to grant or refuse leave to CAG → President; CAG's salary and service conditions determined by Parliament by law (Art 148(3)).

20-056.r: CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Amendment Act, 1976 (in force 1 March 1976) → accounting separated from audit; CAG confined to auditing Government accounts.

20-057.r: Amendment to the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 → made in 1976; separated Accounts from Audit, relieving CAG of preparing accounts.

20-058.r: Accounts of the States (and the Union) → controlled by the CAG; not Governor, CM or State Finance Secretary → 'None of these'.

20-059.r: Guardian of the Public Purse → Comptroller and Auditor General (Art 148); head of Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

20-060.r: CAG → guardian of public finance; ensures no money from Consolidated Fund of India or of a State is spent without the Legislature's authorisation.

20-061.r: Girish Chandra Murmu → 14th CAG of India; K. Sanjay Murthy → 15th CAG (appointed 2024).

20-062.r: Vice-President → Rajya Sabha; CAG → Public Accounts Committee; Solicitor General → Supreme Court; Attorney General → meetings of Lok Sabha.
